<reason>Side B (PRO) won on clash resolution and framing. Its "exit once versus renting the harm" comparison gave voters a clean decision rule, and it turned Side A's own pressure-question answer into support: when A offered a comparative threshold for justified phase-outs, B's closing argued the motion already satisfies it for the most wasteful items — a move A never fully neutralized. A's strongest live route was the asymmetry point (B demands volume evidence for pricing while not proving phase-out reduces total lifecycle harm) plus the sharp circularity attack on B's "safety valve"; but A's honest concession of no evidence that pricing shrinks volumes, combined with a mostly conditional case, left B's narrative more decisive. A was epistemically disciplined and rigorous, but B made the debate easier to decide and answered pressure more directly (clear A1/A2 structure, decisive reframes).</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B4.3–B4.5: PRO conceded continued use after charges is not automatically failure, then redefined failure as growing volumes funded by a receipt line-item, and crystallized that "lighter single-use is still single-use," converting A's pricing remedy into permanent harm-renting versus one-time exit.</best_rebuttal>
